connections.ssh.name: SSH
connections.ssh.sub: {n} host(s) available to agents · manage on the SSH page
connections.ssh.body: Sessions with an SSH-enabled host can run commands and read/write files on it via the ssh_* tools (gated by the session's SSH approval mode). {n} host(s) are currently available to agents. Add or manage hosts — and toggle which are available — on the SSH page.

connections.perms.apiHint: One "METHOD path" per line — path is a regex (e.g. POST /search).

connections.detail.noTools: No tools listed yet — run Test to fetch them.
connections.detail.filterTools: Filter tools by name or description…
connections.detail.oauthWaiting: Complete the authorization in your browser. This window updates automatically.
connections.detail.credentialNote: The credential is stored in the OS keychain and can only be overwritten, never read back. Edit this source to set or replace it.
connections.editor.slugRenameHint: Renames the folder on disk. Stored tokens and agent/session references are kept (they track the internal id, not the slug).
connections.editor.name: Display name
connections.editor.namePh: Name shown in the source list
connections.editor.iconHint: An emoji or an icon URL. A URL falls back to a type icon until download lands.
connections.editor.taglinePh: Short blurb shown to the agent
connections.editor.pathHint: Absolute path or ~-anchored. Access is scoped to this folder.
connections.editor.authTypeHint: How this remote server authenticates. OAuth signs in via your browser; the token is stored in the OS keychain.
connections.editor.oauthHeadersNote: No manual token needed — connect via OAuth from the source detail after saving.
connections.editor.mcpBearerHint: Paste only the token; AWOG sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Stored in the OS keychain — never written to config or git.
connections.editor.mcpBearerHintKeep: Paste only the token; AWOG sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Stored in the OS keychain. Leave blank to keep the existing token.
connections.editor.healthHint: After the handshake, call one read-only tool to confirm the token authenticates. Pick a tool that reads authenticated data — a public tool passes even with a bad token.
connections.editor.healthToolPh: Tool name — run Verify first to list tools
connections.editor.healthArgsInvalid: Args must be a valid JSON object.
connections.editor.baseUrlHint: The API root, e.g. https://api.example.com/ — a trailing slash is recommended.
connections.editor.apiOAuthNote: No manual credential needed — after saving, connect via OAuth from the source detail. The OAuth endpoints are auto-discovered from the base URL.
connections.editor.authSchemeHint: Prefix sent before the token, e.g. "Bearer". Leave empty to send the raw token.
connections.editor.credentialHint: Stored in the OS keychain — never written to config or git.
connections.editor.credentialHintKeep: Stored in the OS keychain — never written to config or git. Leave blank to keep the existing credential.
connections.editor.testEndpointHint: Used by Verify to check the credential works.
connections.editor.testBodyInvalid: Body must be a valid JSON object.
